documents.unit: Office of Academic Affairs; DoIT; Student Success and Enrollment Management
documents.title: HU Policy on the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The policy does not itself ban or require AI; it says students "may use AI tools in accordance with course-specific guidance" and "Faculty determine and communicate course-level AI policies in syllabi and assignments", handing decisions to instructors within university floors (no unauthorized completion of graded work, no Restricted Data). That is delegates.
documents.summary: Board-approved university-wide policy (April 2026) setting principles, definitions, and rules for student, faculty, and administrative AI use. It defers course-level AI rules to faculty while prohibiting unauthorized AI completion of graded work and entry of restricted data. It also covers detectors, human oversight, enforcement and periodic review.

units.why: The Purpose sets the policy's aim as "responsible, ethical, and lawful use of Artificial Intelligence"; an institution-level preamble stating purpose and principles fits P56.
units.anchor: establishes principles and standards for the responsible, ethical, and lawful
units.frag_end: values of integrity, accountability, and fairness.

units.why: The Scope sentence says who the policy binds ("all faculty, staff, students, contractors, and affiliates"); defining scope is P61 rather than P56 because it delimits coverage, not principles.
units.anchor: applies to all faculty, staff, students, contractors, and affiliates who use AI

units.why: The definition of AI ("Machine-based systems that... make predictions, recommendations, or decisions") sets what the policy covers, so P61 with informs.
units.anchor: Machine-based systems that, for a given set of human- defined objectives

units.why: The agentic AI definition ("Autonomous systems powered by large language models") defines a covered tool class; P61.
units.anchor: Autonomous systems powered by large language models (LLMs)

units.why: The generative AI definition explicitly includes "computer code" among generated content, defining scope; P61.
units.anchor: A class of AI systems that generate new content

units.why: The definition of Restricted Data (FERPA, HIPAA, PII) sets what data is protected from AI tools; a scope definition, so P61 rather than P50 which covers the protection duty itself.
units.anchor: Information classified by Hampton University as confidential or sensitive

units.why: The principles open with "AI may be used at Hampton University to enhance learning, teaching, research", a default welcome of AI use; P02, permit.
units.anchor: AI may be used at Hampton University to enhance learning, teaching, research

units.why: "Responsible - users are accountable for outputs they generate or rely upon" makes users answerable for AI output; P29 fits best.
units.anchor: users are accountable for outputs they generate or rely upon

units.why: "Transparent - use of AI is disclosed where appropriate" is a general disclosure principle, P24, hedged so modality should.
units.anchor: use of AI is disclosed where appropriate

units.why: "Ethical - aligned with academic integrity and institutional values" ties all AI use to integrity without stating misconduct handling, so a framework principle P56.
units.anchor: aligned with academic integrity and institutional values

units.why: "Secure - protects sensitive and restricted data" requires data protection in all AI use; P50.
units.anchor: protects sensitive and restricted data

units.why: "Human-centered - decisions remain subject to human judgment and oversight" keeps humans in the loop; P32 fits better than P46 since grades are not mentioned.
units.anchor: decisions remain subject to human judgment and oversight

units.why: "Students may use AI tools in accordance with course-specific guidance" lets course guidance govern student use, deferring to instructors; P04.
units.anchor: Students may use AI tools in accordance with course-specific guidance

units.why: Item 1 permits "brainstorming, outlining, language support, tutoring, and skills development when permitted by the instructor". Several uses are listed; I chose P12 (tutor) as the main fit since P15 and P18 each cover only part, and all are instructor-conditioned.
units.anchor: AI may be used for brainstorming, outlining, language support, tutoring

units.why: Item 2 says "Use of AI to complete assignments, exams, or graded work without authorization is prohibited"; barring AI from producing submitted work absent authorization is P19.
units.anchor: Use of AI to complete assignments, exams, or graded work without authorization

units.why: Item 3 "Students must acknowledge and cite AI use when required" is a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: Students must acknowledge and cite AI use when required

units.why: Item 4 makes students responsible "for verifying the accuracy and integrity of AI-generated content"; P31 verify AI output.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for verifying the accuracy and integrity of AI-generated

units.why: Item 5 "Restricted Data must not be entered into AI tools" protects confidential data; P50 (not P20, which concerns assignment specs and code).
units.anchor: Restricted Data must not be entered into AI tools

units.why: "Violations will be addressed under the Hampton University Student Code of Conduct" sends student AI violations to conduct processes; P36.
units.anchor: Violations will be addressed under the Hampton University Student Code of Conduct

units.why: "Faculty use of AI should uphold academic freedom while ensuring instructional integrity and fairness" is guidance on instructor AI use; P59, modality should.
units.anchor: Faculty use of AI should uphold academic freedom while ensuring instructional integrity

units.why: "Faculty determine and communicate course-level AI policies in syllabi and assignments" requires an AI statement and delegates the rule to faculty; P09 chosen over P04 since the sentence is about communicating it in syllabi.
units.anchor: Faculty determine and communicate course-level AI policies in syllabi and

units.why: "AI detection tools must not be used as the sole basis for academic misconduct determinations" limits reliance on detectors; P39.
units.anchor: AI detection tools must not be used as the sole basis

units.why: "AI may support teaching, assessment design, feedback, and research, with appropriate review for accuracy and bias" states what instructors may use AI for; P59.
units.anchor: AI may support teaching, assessment design, feedback, and research

units.why: "Restricted Data, unpublished student work, and confidential research materials must not be entered into AI systems without DoIT approval" is a faculty data-protection rule; P50.
units.anchor: unpublished student work, and confidential research materials must not be entered into AI systems

units.why: "Faculty are expected to model ethical, transparent, and responsible AI use" sets an expectation on instructors; P47 is disclosure to students and does not fit, so P59 for instructor conduct.
units.anchor: Faculty are expected to model ethical, transparent, and responsible AI use

units.why: "AAI may be used to increase student service operations that support advising, retention, and graduation" permits agentic AI in administration; no type covers non-teaching administrative use (P59 is teaching work), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: AAI may be used to increase student service operations
units.uncovered_note: Permission to use agentic AI in administrative student-service operations (advising, retention); not about teaching or learning.

units.why: Agents "may be used to enhance operational workflows... provided outputs are reviewed for accuracy"; administrative operational use that no type covers.
units.anchor: may be used to enhance operational workflows, communications, data analysis
units.uncovered_note: Conditional permission for AI agents in administrative workflows, with review of outputs.

units.why: "must be reviewed by a human prior to use" requires human review of AI outputs in official operations; closest is P31 verify output.
units.anchor: must be reviewed by a human prior to use
units.frag_end: by a human prior to use

units.why: "AI may not be used to make final decisions regarding employment, finances, academic standing, or disciplinary actions without appropriate human oversight" restricts AI decisions; P46 covers grades only, so P32 human decision-maker.
units.anchor: AI may not be used to make final decisions regarding employment, finances, academic standing

units.why: "Restricted Data must not be entered into AI systems without DoIT approval" repeats the data rule but within administrative use; coded P50 for this section.
units.anchor: Restricted Data must not be entered into AI systems without DoIT approval

units.why: "AI must not be used for discriminatory practices, unauthorized surveillance, or activities that violate law" names harms; P53.
units.anchor: AI must not be used for discriminatory practices, unauthorized surveillance

units.why: "All AI use must comply with Hampton University’s data governance, information security, and acceptable use policies" is a data-protection compliance rule; P50.
units.anchor: All AI use must comply with Hampton University’s data governance, information security

units.why: "Users must consult DoIT prior to using AI tools that process sensitive or restricted data" routes sensitive use through IT review; P50.
units.anchor: Users must consult DoIT prior to using AI tools that process sensitive

units.why: "AI tools may not be used to facilitate academic dishonesty" bans AI-assisted dishonesty; P36 classifies misuse as misconduct, chosen over P19 since it does not mention submitting generated work.
units.anchor: AI tools may not be used to facilitate academic dishonesty
units.frag_start: AI tools may not be used

units.why: The same Prohibited Uses sentence bars use to "violate intellectual property rights"; a distinct rule, P52.
units.anchor: violate intellectual property rights
units.frag_start: AI tools may not be used

units.why: The same sentence bars use to "generate or distribute misinformation" and for "harassment, discrimination"; harms, P53.
units.anchor: generate or distribute misinformation
units.frag_start: AI tools may not be used

units.why: "Violations will be addressed through applicable student, faculty, or staff disciplinary processes" sets enforcement through discipline; P36.
units.anchor: Violations will be addressed through applicable student, faculty, or staff disciplinary

units.why: "The Division of Information Technology may restrict access to AI tools that pose institutional risk" is an institutional control over tools; P50 vetted tools is closest.
units.anchor: may restrict access to AI tools that pose institutional risk

units.why: "will provide ongoing education and professional development to promote responsible AI use" commits support for learning about AI; P63, though the audience is broader than faculty.
units.anchor: will provide ongoing education and professional development to promote responsible AI use

units.why: "This policy will be reviewed periodically by the Office of the Provost" sets a review cycle; P54.
units.anchor: This policy will be reviewed periodically by the Office of the Provost

notes: Task force deck excluded per collect screen. Two administrative-use units are UNCOVERED (no type for non-teaching administrative AI use).
